inputs.label: Beam's own weight, over the span
Rider on left swing, with seat and chain
Rider on right swing, with seat and chain
Chain tension per pound of rider
inputs.basis: Smooth pendulum, from conservation of energy and the centripetal force

inputs.label: Left swing chain tension, W1·(3 − 2·cos θ)
Right swing chain tension, W2·(3 − 2·cos θ)
Beam density at that moisture content

sources.locator: 3.1.3 density formula, p. 12 (corroborating up to 30% moisture content)

assumptions: Supported at the two frame centerlines, 13-3/4" and 106-1/4" from the left end; the span runs center to center of the legs.
Each A-frame holds the beam against rotation at its support (legs bolted against both faces, gusset underneath), so the unbraced length is the span.
The beam's own weight acts as a uniform load over the span, from its density at the entered moisture content; seats and chains are in the rider weights.
Simply supported between the two supports; loads outside the supports, including the weight of any overhang, are not part of this check.
Smooth pendulum: chain tension at the bottom of the arc is W·(3 − 2·cos θ) for a rider of weight W swinging to θ from vertical.
Both swings are at the bottom of their arcs at the same time (riders in sync), so their loads add.
Each swing's load is split equally between its two hangers (a centered rider).
The dynamic factor covers snap loads from slack chains, which exceed the smooth pendulum load. It is not applied to the beam's own weight.
formulas: R1 = Σ P·(L − a) / L + w·L / 2, R2 = Σ P·a / L + w·L / 2 (a = distance of each load from the left support)
M(x) = R1·x − w·x² / 2 − Σ P·(x − a) over loads left of x; the largest M is where the shear changes sign
S = b·d² / 6
f_b = M / S
Fb' = Fb · C_D · C_M · C_t · C_L · C_F · C_fu · C_i · C_r
margin = Fb' / f_b

steps.label: Fb with all factors except C_L and C_fu

factors.name: Load duration
factors.reason: Ten years (occupancy live load). C_D = 1.0: the impact increase is not used, and factors above 1.6 do not apply to lumber treated with water-borne preservatives (NDS 4.3.13).

factors.name: Wet service
factors.reason: The beam is outdoors and uncovered, so its moisture content can stay above 19%. Fb·C_F = 1000 psi, at or below 1150 psi, so C_M = 1.0 for Fb.

checklist.element: Leg-to-beam bolt and gusset, each frame
checklist.confirm: Bolt size (1/2" entered, 8-15/16" grip), edge and end distances in the legs and beam, washers on the tilted outer faces, and that the gusset and bolt together carry the beam's reaction.
checklist.why: Each frame carries half of every swing load into the legs through this joint; connections are not computed.

checklist.confirm: That each frame holds the beam against rolling over at its support.
checklist.why: The beam stability factor assumes it; without that restraint the beam can buckle sideways at a lower load.

checklist.confirm: That the frames resist side-to-side and front-to-back swing forces without racking, and whether corner braces are needed.
checklist.why: Swinging pushes the top of the frame back and forth; racking is not computed.

checklist.confirm: Burial depth (24"), soil, backfill or concrete, and lumber rated for ground contact.
checklist.why: Burial keeps the frame from lifting and walking; tipping and anchoring are not computed.

checklist.confirm: Hangers rated for swing use, installed through the beam as the manufacturer specifies.
checklist.why: The hanger margin uses the manufacturer's rating, which holds only for its specified installation.

checklist.confirm: Boards free of large knots near the edges (especially near midspan of the beam), steep grain slope, splits, and wane.
checklist.why: Design values assume the grade; a defect in the wrong place lowers strength more than the grade allows for.

checklist.confirm: An inspection routine: nuts and bolts twice a month, seats and chains monthly (CPSC Pub. 324, p. 5), and decay at the ground line.
checklist.why: Wood shrinks and bolts loosen, especially in pressure-treated lumber that was sold wet.

assumptions: Each ply carries an equal share of every load (decision 0013).
Supported at the two frame centerlines, 13-3/4" and 106-1/4" from the left end; the span runs center to center of the legs.
Each A-frame holds the beam against rotation at its support (legs bolted against both faces, gusset underneath), so the unbraced length is the span.
The beam's own weight acts as a uniform load over the span, from its density at the entered moisture content; seats and chains are in the rider weights.
Simply supported between the two supports; loads outside the supports, including the weight of any overhang, are not part of this check.
Smooth pendulum: chain tension at the bottom of the arc is W·(3 − 2·cos θ) for a rider of weight W swinging to θ from vertical.
Both swings are at the bottom of their arcs at the same time (riders in sync), so their loads add.
Each swing's load is split equally between its two hangers (a centered rider).
The dynamic factor covers snap loads from slack chains, which exceed the smooth pendulum load. It is not applied to the beam's own weight.
formulas: Load per ply = P / n and w / n
R1 = Σ P·(L − a) / L + w·L / 2, R2 = Σ P·a / L + w·L / 2 (a = distance of each load from the left support)
M(x) = R1·x − w·x² / 2 − Σ P·(x − a) over loads left of x; the largest M is where the shear changes sign
S = b·d² / 6
f_b = M / S
Fb' = Fb · C_D · C_M · C_t · C_L · C_F · C_fu · C_i · C_r
margin = Fb' / f_b

checklist.element: Leg-to-beam bolt and gusset, each frame
checklist.confirm: Bolt size (1/2" entered, 8-7/16" grip), edge and end distances in the legs and beam, washers on the tilted outer faces, and that the gusset and bolt together carry the beam's reaction.
checklist.why: Each frame carries half of every swing load into the legs through this joint; connections are not computed.

checklist.confirm: Ply bolt pattern and spacing (6 bolts entered), and that every hanger bolts through all 2 plies.
checklist.why: The checks assume each ply carries an equal share of every load (decision 0013); that holds only if the plies are fastened together and every load reaches every ply.

checklist.confirm: That each frame holds the beam against rolling over at its support.
checklist.why: The beam stability factor assumes it; without that restraint the beam can buckle sideways at a lower load.

checklist.confirm: That the frames resist side-to-side and front-to-back swing forces without racking, and whether corner braces are needed.
checklist.why: Swinging pushes the top of the frame back and forth; racking is not computed.

checklist.confirm: Anchor type and count (1 per foot) and how they are buried or covered.
checklist.why: Anchors keep the frame from lifting, tipping, and walking; tipping and anchoring are not computed.

checklist.confirm: Hangers rated for swing use, installed through the beam as the manufacturer specifies.
checklist.why: The hanger margin uses the manufacturer's rating, which holds only for its specified installation.

checklist.confirm: Boards free of large knots near the edges (especially near midspan of the beam), steep grain slope, splits, and wane.
checklist.why: Design values assume the grade; a defect in the wrong place lowers strength more than the grade allows for.

checklist.confirm: An inspection routine: nuts and bolts twice a month, seats and chains monthly (CPSC Pub. 324, p. 5), and decay at the ground line.
checklist.why: Wood shrinks and bolts loosen, especially in pressure-treated lumber that was sold wet.
